references.text: Jesus gives similar instructions to the twelve disciples to shake the dust off their feet as a testimony against those who do not receive them.
Paul and Barnabas shook the dust from their feet against the inhabitants of Antioch in Pisidia, in accordance with Jesus' command to do this as a sign of judgment.
Paul shook the dust from his clothes as a testimony against the Jews in Corinth who opposed him, an action with the same symbolic meaning.
In Matthew's parallel account, Jesus instructs the twelve to shake the dust off their feet when leaving a city that does not receive them, warning of the coming judgment.
Mark's parallel where Jesus instructs the disciples to shake the dust from their feet as a testimony against those who reject the message.
The preceding instruction in the same speech where the disciples are to proclaim that the kingdom of God has come near—the same message repeated in verse 11 as a warning.
John the Baptist proclaimed the same message: "Guds rike er kommet nær", which is here repeated as a warning to those who reject the disciples.
Jesus himself began his preaching with the words "Guds rike er kommet nær", the same message that the disciples are now to proclaim even to those who reject them.
The following verse elaborates on the judgment awaiting the city that rejects the disciples' message, stating it will be better for Sodom on that day.
